transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I feel like if I don’t keep really tight control over what I eat, I’ll gain weight and everything I’ve worked for will fall apart. My campus advisor and doctor strongly encouraged me to come here, but that's really what's constantly on my mind.
To help me understand your physical health, could you tell me your current height and weight, and whether you've recently lost a significant amount of weight?

I don't really want to focus on the exact numbers, but my resident advisor and campus doctor keep saying I've gotten "so thin" and have lost a lot of weight. My clothes are definitely hanging off me now, even though I don't think it's as extreme as they make it out to be.
Do you ever experience episodes where you eat an unusually large amount of food in a short period of time and feel like you cannot stop or control your eating?
No, I don't experience anything like that at all. My focus is entirely on keeping very strict control over the small amount I do eat. I would never let myself lose control or overeat like that.
Aside from restricting your food, do you ever use other methods to control your weight, such as making yourself throw up, using laxatives, or exercising excessively?
No, I've never done anything like that—no throwing up, laxatives, or crazy workouts. I only rely on strictly controlling and restricting what I eat to keep everything under control.
How much does your body weight or shape influence how you judge your self-worth or feel about yourself as a person?

It honestly dictates everything about how I feel. If the scale goes down, I feel worthy of being in the honors program and pursuing my dream of becoming an art therapist. But if it goes up even half a pound, I feel completely disgusting and like I don't deserve to be in any of my roles on campus.
Have you noticed any physical changes like your menstrual periods stopping or becoming irregular, or a significant decrease in your sex drive?
I'm not really sure, as I haven't paid much attention to that lately. I've been so overwhelmed with my classes and keeping up with my routines that I haven't really thought about it.
Could you tell me when you had your last menstrual period, or if you are currently taking any hormonal contraceptives like birth control pills?
I'm really not sure when my last period was, as I haven't kept track of it at all lately. I'm also not taking any birth control pills or other contraceptives.
Has your campus doctor or another healthcare provider specifically told you that your current weight is clinically underweight or below the normal range for your height?

Yes, the campus doctor did tell me I'm underweight and even brought up concerns about my heart and bones, mentioning a potential medical leave. But it honestly feels completely blown out of proportion because I’m still walking to all my classes, getting straight A's, and I don’t feel nearly sick enough to warrant that kind of extreme reaction.
Even if you haven't kept close track, do you recall if you've had a menstrual period at all in the last three months?
I honestly don't remember if I've had one in the last three months. I've just been so completely focused on my classes and my daily routines that I haven't paid any attention to it.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with significant self-induced weight loss, intensive restriction of food intake, an extreme fear of gaining weight, and a self-evaluation that is disproportionately influenced by body weight and shape. Her campus doctor has confirmed she is clinically underweight with physical health concerns (heart and bone issues). Although amenorrhea could not be definitively confirmed due to the patient's lack of tracking, the overall clinical picture of severe restriction, underweight status, and body image distortion strongly supports a diagnosis of Anorexia Nervosa (F50.0), with Atypical Anorexia Nervosa (F50.1) considered as the key differential due to the unconfirmed menstrual status.
